stem: What does the term 'hadith' refer to?
options: A verse of the Quran revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) through Jibreel (AS)
A report of the sayings, actions or approvals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
A ruling given by a judge
explanation: A hadith is a narration of what the Prophet (PBUH) said, did, or approved. The Quran is the revealed Word of Allah and is distinct from hadith.

stem: The word 'Sunnah' means
options: the way and example of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
a recitation of the Quran in the five daily prayers
explanation: Sunnah is the practical example and way of life of the Prophet (PBUH). It is the second source of guidance after the Quran.

stem: Who compiled Sahih al-Bukhari?
explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari was compiled by Imam al-Bukhari. Muslim compiled Sahih Muslim, Tirmidhi the Jami', and Malik the Muwatta.

stem: Sahih Muslim was compiled by
explanation: Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj of Nishapur compiled Sahih Muslim, which is ranked with Sahih al-Bukhari as the most authentic collections.

stem: The two collections together known as the 'Sahihayn' are
options: Sunan Abu Dawud and Sunan an-Nasa'i
Jami' at-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah
explanation: 'Sahihayn' means 'the two Sahihs', referring to the collections of Bukhari and Muslim.

stem: Which of the following is one of the Six Books (Kutub al-Sittah) of hadith?
explanation: Sunan Abu Dawud is one of the six major collections. Riyad as-Salihin is a later compilation by Imam an-Nawawi, and the other two are works of other kinds.

stem: Jami' at-Tirmidhi was compiled by
explanation: The Jami' bears the name of its compiler, Imam Muhammad ibn Isa at-Tirmidhi. Each of the others compiled a different collection.

stem: Al-Muwatta, one of the earliest hadith books, was compiled in Madinah by
explanation: Imam Malik compiled Al-Muwatta in Madinah. Imam Ahmad compiled the Musnad, and Nawawi lived centuries later.

stem: Who compiled the large collection known as Musnad?
explanation: The Musnad is the work of Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It contains a very large number of hadith arranged by narrator.

stem: Imam al-Bukhari was born in which city, from which he takes his name?
explanation: He was born in Bukhara in Central Asia, and the name al-Bukhari means 'of Bukhara'. He later travelled widely to collect hadith.

stem: Which companion narrated the largest number of hadith?
explanation: Abu Hurayrah (RA) is the best known for the greatest number of narrations. Anas and Ibn Umar also narrated many, but fewer.

stem: Which wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) narrated the largest number of hadith?
explanation: Aisha (RA) narrated well over two thousand hadith and was a great scholar of the community. Khadijah (RA) passed away before the Hijrah.

stem: In hadith terminology, the 'isnad' is
explanation: Isnad is the chain of narrators through whom a hadith reached the compiler. The text itself is the matn.

stem: The text or content of a hadith is called
explanation: Matn is the text of the report. The chain of narrators is the isnad (or sanad), and a narrator is a rawi.

stem: A narrator of a hadith is called
explanation: A rawi is one who narrates a hadith. A mufassir explains the Quran, and a qari recites it.

stem: A hadith whose chain or narrators have a weakness that keeps it from the standard of authenticity is called
explanation: Da'if means weak. Sahih is authentic, mutawatir is reported by so many that error is impossible, and Qudsi refers to a report with words from Allah.

stem: What is a Hadith Qudsi?
options: A report in which the Prophet (PBUH) relates a saying of Allah in his own words
A verse of the Quran that describes the events of the hereafter
A hadith about the city of Jerusalem
explanation: In a Hadith Qudsi the meaning is from Allah, conveyed in the Prophet's own words. Unlike the Quran, its wording is not recited in prayer.

stem: A collection of hadith arranged according to the companion who narrated them is called a
explanation: In a Musnad, hadith are grouped under each Sahabi. A Sunan is organised by legal topics such as prayer and purification.

stem: A companion did something in the presence of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who did not object. This approval is called
explanation: Taqrir is the silent approval of the Prophet (PBUH). Qawl is his saying and fi'l his action.

stem: After the Quran, what is the second source of guidance in Islam?
options: The personal writings of later historians and poets
Opinions of any scholar of any period
The Sunnah of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
explanation: Muslims are guided first by the Quran and then by the Sunnah, which explains and applies it.

stem: Which hadith is placed at the very beginning of Sahih al-Bukhari?
explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari opens with the hadith that actions are judged by intentions, a basic principle for all deeds.

stem: The hadith 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself' teaches
options: strict fasting on every day of the week
explanation: This well-known hadith (Bukhari and Muslim) makes goodwill towards others a part of true faith.

stem: According to a well-known hadith, who is truly strong?
options: The one who wins every contest of strength
The one who owns the most wealth
The one who speaks the loudest
The one who controls himself when angry
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that real strength lies in self-control at the time of anger, not in overpowering others.

stem: A hadith describes a true Muslim as one from whose tongue and hands
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said a Muslim is the one from whose tongue and hands other Muslims are safe, stressing good conduct.

stem: A well-known hadith advises the believer in Allah and the Last Day to
options: speak at length on every matter
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that one who believes in Allah and the Last Day should say what is good or else remain silent.

stem: When asked who most deserved his good companionship, the Prophet (PBUH) first replied
explanation: He answered 'your mother' three times before mentioning the father, showing the high status of mothers (Bukhari and Muslim).

stem: Which of the following continues to benefit a person after death, according to a well-known hadith?
options: Wealth he left unspent in the bank
A righteous child who prays for him
explanation: The hadith lists ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge and a righteous child who makes dua. Worldly possessions are not counted.

stem: The hadith 'Cleanliness is half of faith' emphasises
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said cleanliness is half of faith, a teaching that includes cleanliness of body, clothing and surroundings.

stem: According to a hadith on the branches of faith, the lowest branch is
options: removing something harmful from the road
feeding the poor at every meal
explanation: The hadith says the highest is saying La ilaha illallah and the lowest is removing something harmful from the path. Modesty is also a branch of faith.

stem: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that Jibreel (AS) kept advising him about whom, until he thought they might be made heirs?
explanation: The hadith (Bukhari and Muslim) shows the great importance of the rights of neighbours.

stem: In a well-known hadith, the Prophet (PBUH) said 'The religion is nasihah'. This means
explanation: Nasihah means sincere advice and sincerity towards Allah, His Book, His Messenger, leaders and the common Muslims.

stem: According to a hadith, who are the best among the people?
options: Those who learn the Quran and teach it
Those who have gathered the most wealth in life
Those who have the most followers
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said the best among you are those who learn the Quran and teach it (Bukhari).

stem: Which of these is a sign of a hypocrite mentioned in a well-known hadith?
options: When he is asked, he gives charity
When he fasts, he is hungry
When he travels, he prays short prayers
explanation: The hadith says that when a hypocrite speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when trusted he betrays. The others are ordinary acts.

stem: A hadith says that whoever does not show mercy to others
options: will gain more wealth in this world
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said the one who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy (Bukhari and Muslim).

stem: The Prophet (PBUH) advised his companions to
options: avoid giving good news to the people
make things easy and not difficult
explanation: He instructed that things be made easy and that people be given glad tidings, not made to run away.

stem: In the Hadith of Jibreel, the Prophet (PBUH) explained 'ihsan' as
options: performing Hajj every year without fail
worshipping Allah as if you see Him
explanation: In the Hadith of Jibreel, ihsan is to worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, He sees you.

stem: The Hadith of Jibreel, describing Islam, iman and ihsan, is narrated in Sahih Muslim by
explanation: It is narrated from Umar (RA), who described the stranger in white clothes who asked the Prophet (PBUH) questions.

stem: The hadith 'Islam is built upon five' is reported in Bukhari and Muslim from which companion?
explanation: This hadith about the five pillars is narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar (RA).

stem: Who compiled the well-known collection of 'Forty Hadith' (Al-Arba'in)?
explanation: Imam Yahya ibn Sharaf an-Nawawi compiled the Forty Hadith, which cover basic principles of the faith.

stem: According to a hadith, for one who travels a path seeking knowledge, Allah
options: makes easy a path to Paradise
removes all hardship from the world
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said that Allah eases the path to Paradise for one who seeks knowledge (Sahih Muslim).

stem: The Prophet (PBUH) said that charity does not
explanation: The hadith (Muslim) states that giving charity does not reduce wealth, as Allah blesses what is given.

stem: A 'Sahabi' is
options: any scholar who has narrated hadith in later times
a person who lived in Madinah in the time of the Prophet (PBUH)
a person who met the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as a believer and died as a believer
explanation: A Sahabi is one who met the Prophet (PBUH), believed in him, and died on that faith.

stem: A 'Tabi'i' (successor) is
options: a person who lived in Makkah
a person who met a companion of the Prophet (PBUH) as a believer
a person who compiled the Quran
a person who saw the Prophet (PBUH) only once in a dream
explanation: A Tabi'i is from the generation after the companions who met them as a believer. Meeting the Prophet (PBUH) himself makes one a Sahabi.

stem: A hadith reported by so many narrators in every generation that agreement on a falsehood is impossible is called
explanation: This is the highest level of reliability. Da'if is weak, mawdu' is fabricated, and mursal has a missing companion in the chain.

stem: A hadith falsely attributed to the Prophet (PBUH) is called
explanation: A fabricated report is mawdu' and must be rejected. Attributing falsehood to the Prophet (PBUH) is a serious sin.

stem: The Prophet (PBUH) said he was sent to
options: build large cities and grand palaces
explanation: The well-known meaning of the hadith is that he was sent to complete good morals.

stem: According to a hadith, honesty leads to
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness to Paradise (Bukhari and Muslim).

stem: The Prophet (PBUH) said 'The upper hand is better than the lower hand.' This means
options: the strong are the best rulers over the weak
the tall are better than the short
the one who gives is better than the one who takes
the early riser is better than the sleeper
explanation: The upper hand is the giving hand, encouraging charity and self-reliance.

stem: A hadith lists those whom Allah will shade on the Day when there is no other shade. Who is among them?
options: A wealthy trader who gave nothing
A person who prayed only in public
One who judged by his own desires
explanation: The hadith in Bukhari and Muslim begins with the just ruler and mentions a youth growing up in worship. The other options describe the opposite of such qualities.

stem: A hadith states that Allah does not look at your appearance and wealth but at
options: your family lines and tribal status
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) taught that what matters before Allah is the heart and actions (Sahih Muslim).

stem: A kind word, according to a hadith, is
explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said a good word is sadaqah, so even those without wealth can give charity.

stem: In which city did Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj live and work, from which he is known as an-Naysaburi?
explanation: Imam Muslim belonged to Nishapur, in the Persian region of Khurasan, which gives him the name an-Naysaburi.
